scope: Full residential asphalt-shingle roof replacement (tear-off + reroof). Excludes new construction, low-slope membrane, tile, and slate (categories present but stubbed for future expansion).
structure_notes: Materials and labor are tracked separately to support regional margin tuning. Quote = (material_cost + labor_cost) / (1 - target_gross_margin) + permits + dumpster. Apply regional multipliers to material_cost and labor_cost BEFORE the margin uplift. See pricing.md for the full formula and worked example.

materials._units: All `cost_per_*` fields are MATERIAL ONLY at contractor (wholesale) cost — labor lives in the `labor` block below. Prices are 2026 baseline; apply regional.material_multiplier.

shingles_field._unit: per square (100 sqft of roof area, before waste)

asphalt_class4_impact._comment: Insurance discount common in CO/TX hail belt.

asphalt_cool_roof._comment: Required for low-slope sections under CA Title 24; popular in AZ/NV.

starter_strip._comment: Some crews cut field shingles instead. Spec'd starter is cleaner and required for full warranty.

ice_water_shield.applies_to: eaves (3 ft from edge), valleys (full width), penetrations, low-slope sections

step_flashing_aluminum._unit: per piece (4x5x7), one per shingle course at sidewalls

pipe_boot_lead._comment: Lasts longer; spec for FL HVHZ

kickout_flashing._comment: Where roof meets sidewall above gutter — code in many jurisdictions

chimney_flashing_kit._comment: Includes apron, step, counter, saddle if needed

box_vent_static._comment: Rule of thumb: 1 vent per 300 sqft of attic if no ridge vent

soffit_vent_continuous._comment: Usually existing; budget if soffit work is in scope

decking._comment: Replacement decking is a contingency line item — budget 3–8% of deck area for typical reroof. Bill actual sheets used.

plywood_cdx_5_8._comment: Required code minimum in some FL HVHZ counties

hurricane_clip._comment: Required in FL HVHZ; one per truss bearing

labor._units: All rates are LABOR ONLY (crew time, not material). Apply regional.labor_multiplier before margin uplift.

single_layer_per_sqft._comment: Crew labor only. Excludes dumpster (separate). HomeGuide 2026: $25–50/sq for tear-off labor.

triple_layer_per_sqft._comment: Rare; usually code violation that demands tear-off.

asphalt_per_sqft._comment: Crew labor only. Includes underlayment install, starter, and field shingle nailing. HomeGuide 2026: $150–300/sq for shingle labor.

steep_slope_premium_pct._comment: Adds 20% to labor portion for harnesses + slow production

two_story_premium_pct._comment: Optional — some markets price this in

valley_w_metal._comment: Includes ice & water under valley + metal install

decking_replacement_per_sheet._comment: On top of sheet material cost.

satellite_dish_reset._comment: Detach + reattach a customer-owned satellite dish that's mounted on the roof.

supervision_overhead_pct._comment: Foreman / PM / drive time. Apply as % of crew labor. NOT margin — this is a real cost.

demo_disposal._comment: Tear-off LABOR is in labor.tear_off above. This block is the equipment/disposal side.

tipping_fee_overage_per_ton._comment: If weight exceeds dumpster allowance — typical limit 2–3 tons per 20-yard.

permit_per_sqft._comment: Some jurisdictions charge $0.10–0.20/sqft instead of flat. Check local.

regional._comment: Three layers, applied in order: (1) zone defaults by state, (2) state_labor_index refines labor cost from BLS OEWS roofer wages, (3) metro_overrides supersede zone+state for specific MSAs / counties where labor or insurance markets diverge from the state norm. See lib/regional.ts for the merge logic.

low_cost_competitive._comment: High contractor density, retail/cash-pay dominant. Lean on margin to stay competitive.

high_cost_insurance_heavy._comment: Insurance restoration drives volume; retail margins held higher because most jobs are insurance-paid at industry-standard pricing.

premium_metro._comment: High labor cost, fewer reroofs per crew per week, less price-sensitive customer base.

state_labor_index._comment: Multiplier applied to zone labor_multiplier. Grounded in BLS OEWS May 2024 mean wage for SOC 47-2181 (Roofers) by state, normalized to national mean = 1.00. States not listed default to 1.00.

metro_overrides.label: Bay Area
metro_overrides._comment: Premium-of-premium labor market; permitting + landfill fees among highest in the nation.

metro_overrides.label: Denver-Boulder Front Range
metro_overrides._comment: Hail-belt insurance market; volume keeps margins healthy even with strong competition.

metro_overrides.label: Houston metro
metro_overrides._comment: High-volume reroof market; aggressive bidding compresses margin even though labor is reasonable.

metro_overrides.label: Miami-Dade HVHZ
metro_overrides._comment: HVHZ code adds ring-shank fasteners + secondary water barrier + hurricane clips. Material premium rolls into multiplier; labor reflects HVHZ inspection workflow.

code_requirements._comment: Drives material selection. Tool should auto-promote default material when address falls in a flagged zone.

recommends: asphalt_class4_impact for insurance discount (typical 20–30% premium savings)

cold_climate_ice_dam.applies_to: states with avg Jan temp <= 25°F (MN, WI, MI UP, NY upstate, ME, VT, NH, ND, SD, MT, ID, AK)
requires: ice_water_shield extending 24 inches inside warm wall line at eaves (IRC R905.1.2)
cool_roof reflective shingles on low-slope sections, sometimes whole roof

regional_incentives.label: Class 4 wind/hail discount (TX)
regional_incentives.headline: Class 4 typically saves $400–$700/yr on TX homeowner's insurance
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: Texas mandates that insurers file a Class 4 (UL 2218) discount. Most carriers — State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, USAA — land at 20–25% off the wind/hail portion of premium, with the full filed range 15–30%. Use the savings math to make the upgrade pay back in ~5 years.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: Texas mandates that home insurance carriers file a discount for UL 2218 Class 4 impact-resistant shingles. Most carriers in TX (including State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, USAA) discount the wind/hail portion of your premium between 15% and 30% — most landing at 20–25%.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical $3,500/yr premium where roughly 60% is wind/hail coverage, a 25% discount saves about $525/yr. That recovers the upgrade-from-architectural cost in ~5 years and continues to save you money every year after.
regional_incentives.action_step: Call your insurance agent before we schedule the job. Ask for the exact discount percentage and whether they need a shingle-wrapper photo or just the manufacturer's Class 4 certification for the file.

regional_incentives.label: Class 4 hail discount (CO)
regional_incentives.headline: Class 4 typically saves 10–30% on CO homeowner's premium
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: Colorado is one of the most aggressive Class 4 discount markets in the country. Allstate, State Farm, USAA, and American Family all offer it. Front Range hail frequency means insurers often default to non-renewal on roofs without impact-resistant coverage.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: Colorado homeowner's insurance carriers offer a 10–30% premium discount for UL 2218 Class 4 impact-resistant shingles. With the Front Range's hail frequency, insurers actively reward upgrading — and sometimes require it.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical $2,800/yr premium, a 20% discount saves about $560/yr. The Class 4 upgrade typically pays itself back in 4–7 years.
regional_incentives.action_step: Bring the Class 4 manufacturer certification to your insurance agent for the file. Ask about non-renewal protection — most Class 4 policies include it.

regional_incentives.label: Class 4 hail discount (OK)

State Farm, Allstate, American Family, Farmers, Shelter, and Farm Bureau all offer it. OK is in the absolute heart of Tornado Alley — many carriers won't even renew non-Class 4 roofs after a hail loss.

regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical $2,800/yr OK premium where ~65% is wind/hail coverage, a 20% discount saves about $364/yr. The Class 4 upgrade typically pays back in 5–7 years and protects against post-loss non-renewal.
regional_incentives.action_step: Bring the manufacturer's Class 4 certification to your insurance agent. Some carriers also want photos of the shingle-bundle wrapper showing the UL2218 stamp.

regional_incentives.label: Class 4 + wind-mitigation discount (VA)
regional_incentives.headline: VA carriers offer roof-related discounts via Class 4 OR wind-mitigation
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: Virginia is more wind-mitigation focused than hail-belt, but Class 4 still has carrier offerings. State Farm, Liberty Mutual, USAA, and Allstate offer Class 4 discounts of 10–15% on the wind/hail portion. Newport News and tidewater VA also benefit from wind-mitigation inspections.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: Virginia homeowner's carriers offer roof-related premium discounts in two ways: (1) Class 4 impact-resistant shingles save 10–15% on the wind/hail portion via State Farm, Liberty Mutual, USAA, and Allstate; (2) tidewater / coastal VA homes can also schedule a wind-mitigation inspection after the new roof is installed for additional credit on the wind portion.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical $1,800/yr VA premium where ~40% is wind/hail coverage, a 12% Class 4 discount saves about $86/yr. Coastal homes layering wind-mitigation credit can push that to 20–30%.
regional_incentives.action_step: For Class 4: send the manufacturer certification to your agent. For tidewater addresses: also schedule a wind-mitigation inspection within 30 days of completion to layer credits.

regional_incentives.label: Class 4 or FORTIFIED discount (GA)
regional_incentives.headline: GA offers either Class 4 or IBHS FORTIFIED-Roof discounts
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: Georgia carriers offer two roof-related discount paths: Class 4 (State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, Liberty Mutual — 10–20% on wind/hail) OR IBHS FORTIFIED-Roof certification (better for coastal/wind-driven homes). FORTIFIED requires a certified installer and an inspection during install — can't be retrofit.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: Georgia carriers reward better roofs in two ways: (1) UL 2218 Class 4 impact-resistant shingles get a 10–20% discount via State Farm, Allstate, Farmers, and Liberty Mutual; (2) IBHS FORTIFIED-Roof certification (better for coastal and tornado-belt areas) earns separate credits from carriers like Allstate.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical $2,100/yr GA premium where ~50% is wind/hail coverage, a 15% Class 4 discount saves about $158/yr. FORTIFIED can stack additional savings.
regional_incentives.action_step: Pick one path: for inland properties, Class 4 is simpler — just send the manufacturer certification. For coastal or wind-prone zones, ask your contractor about FORTIFIED-Roof certification (must be done during install).

regional_incentives.label: Florida wind-mitigation insurance credit
regional_incentives.headline: Post-replacement wind mitigation can cut FL premium 20–45%
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: After roof replacement, an OIR-1802 wind-mitigation inspection documents roof shape, deck attachment, secondary water barrier, and opening protection. Properly compliant Class 4 + 6-nail pattern + sealed deck typically yields 20–45% reduction on the wind portion of premium. Florida law mandates the credit if the inspection shows compliance.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: Florida law requires homeowner's insurance carriers to give you a credit on the wind portion of your premium when you can document specific roof improvements. After replacement, schedule a wind-mitigation inspection (OIR-1802 form) — verified compliance typically reduces your wind premium by 20–45%.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: On a typical FL coastal premium of $4,500/yr where wind is ~70% of the policy, a 30% wind credit saves about $945/yr.
regional_incentives.action_step: After the job, hire a Florida-certified wind-mitigation inspector ($75–150). Submit the OIR-1802 form to your insurance carrier within 30 days for retroactive credit on your current policy term.

regional_incentives.label: IBHS FORTIFIED Roof certification
regional_incentives.headline: FORTIFIED certification mandates insurance discounts in some Gulf states
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: IBHS FORTIFIED Roof is an above-code standard. AL, MS, LA, SC, NC explicitly mandate insurance discounts for FORTIFIED-certified roofs in coastal counties. AL coastal homeowners can see 35%+ wind premium reduction.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: The IBHS FORTIFIED Roof standard goes above building code. Several states in your region mandate that insurers offer a discount for FORTIFIED-certified roofs. Inspection and certification cost ~$500–800; the standard adds ~$1,000–2,000 to a typical reroof.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: AL coastal: 35% wind premium reduction is typical. On a $4,000/yr coastal policy, that's $1,000+/yr savings.
regional_incentives.action_step: Ask your contractor whether they're a FORTIFIED-certified installer. The certification has to happen during the install — can't be retrofit.

regional_incentives.label: California cool-roof rebate
regional_incentives.headline: Cool-roof shingles can earn utility rebates in CA + cooling-cost savings
regional_incentives.description_for_contractor: Some CA utilities (PG&E, SCE, LADWP) offer rebates around $0.10–0.30/sqft for ENERGY STAR-rated cool-roof shingles. Title 24 mandates cool-roof on low-slope sections.
regional_incentives.description_for_customer: California's Title 24 building energy code requires cool-roof shingles on low-slope roof sections; full cool-roof installation often qualifies for utility rebates ($0.10–0.30/sqft) and reduces summer cooling costs by 7–15%.
regional_incentives.savings_math_template: For a 2,500 sqft roof, a $0.20/sqft rebate is $500. Cooling-cost reduction of 10% on a $1,800/yr summer bill is another ~$180/yr.
regional_incentives.action_step: Check your utility's rebate program and confirm the shingle product is ENERGY STAR-rated before installation.
